statement: Our recognition algorithm for proper tree-graphs provides the following side result on proper leafage (introduced by Lin et al. [21] analogously to leafage): The proper leafage `? of a chordal graph G is the minimum number of leaf nodes of all trees T that properly represent G. The side result, as in Corollary 24, is that computing the proper leafage is FPT. For the decision version, if G is not a proper interval graph, we simply guess the host tree Tsub of minimal leafage and verify properness with our algorithm from Theorem 1. Of course, it still remains open whether computing proper leafage is NP-hard.
